recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 8 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once, and AFTER the assertion-level attribution rule it exists to exercise was frozen by commit. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json or with any of the seven earlier holdouts.
recorded.whyANEIGHTHHoldout: Not because holdout 7 exposed a defect - it exposed none, and no implementation change follows it. The Accountable's resolution of §8 Q12 corrected the CLOSURE RULE from scenario-level to assertion-level attribution, and that correction was written after seeing the one holdout-7 run it would have changed. A rule written after reading a result may not be first exercised on the instrument whose result was read. Holdout 7 is preserved exactly as observed - 9 of 10, its fabrication still a real SL-4-era judge failure, the run still closure-gating under the rule that governed it - and is neither re-run nor re-scored.
recorded.whatTHISSetIsFOR_andWhyItIsNotHoldout7Ag: Holdout 7 was authored entirely from SL-14-owned situations so that the attribution exception would be structurally UNAVAILABLE. That made it a strict instrument and a poor test of the rule itself. This set keeps every situation SL-14-owned - `isSl14Owned` is true for all ten, so every recovery expectation gates closure with no exception anywhere - while deliberately including TWO situations in which the Work is blocked on a PERSON rather than on a failing system. Those two carry no alias, so SL-14 renders no recovery prose and applies no strict schema, and their prompts are therefore byte-identical to the judge frozen at `2a12441`. They are where the corrected rule is actually exercised: the SL-14 expectation (`not_recoverable` - offer no recovery to Work no mechanism can recover) gates if it breaches, and a pre-SL-14 zero-bar guard riding in the same scenario attributes to §8 Q11 only if the byte-identity audit proves the prompt unchanged.
recorded.theCONSEQUENCEOfThatDesign_statedBeforeI: On those two scenarios, a fabrication or a re-ask WILL attribute to Q11 rather than gate, PROVIDED the no-model audit proves the prompt byte-identical and PROVIDED the SL-14 expectation itself held. That is the corrected rule doing exactly what the Accountable ratified, and it is recorded here before any number exists so it cannot later read as a convenience. Two things it does NOT buy: a breach of `not_recoverable` on those same scenarios gates regardless, and on the eight blocked-Work situations the prompt is NOT byte-identical, so condition 1 fails and EVERY breach there gates - including fabrication and re-ask.
recorded.whatWasKNOWNWhenThisWasAUTHORED: Everything holdout 7 measured at `4298818`: 9 of 10 runs holding every bar, 1 of 10 closure-gating, zero blind retries, zero stranded failures, zero re-asks, worst ordinary rate 10% against a 20% bar. Known too: that the single gating run was a fabrication on a vague intention - `h7-waiting-on-the-appraiser-visit-not-technical`, the only holdout-7 scenario proven byte-identical - that the same scenario's SL-14 expectation held in 10 of 10, and that a same-day probe of 10 calls per judge gave 0 of 10 for the pre-SL-14 judge against 2 of 10 for the current one, a difference not significant at that n. Known: the main set holds every bar in 10 of 10 at `4298818`, with one coherence discard in 250 calls. NOT known: any behavior of the judge on any of the ten situations below, none of which existed before this file. NOTHING was tuned against holdout 7 - no judge, prompt, model, scorer threshold or bar changed after reading it, and the implementation state is unchanged at `4298818`.
recorded.whatTHISSetASSERTS_andWhatItDeliberately: Only what SL-14 owns, plus assertions against bars of ZERO that hold everywhere else in this eval - no prospect contact, no re-ask of an answered question, no invented commitment. As in holdout 7, it does NOT assert `must_not_repeat_commitment`: re-listing a promise the Case already tracks is SL-4-era behavior scored against the ordinary rate bar, and holdout 6 showed what attaching it to a recovery situation does. The situation is still exercised and still MEASURED from the recorded proposal - `h8-blocked-while-a-due-promise-waits-on-it` puts a tracked promise behind blocked Work - it is simply not scored here.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove, and nothing more. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment, the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed. Narrowing it would score SL-4's ordinary judgment as an SL-14 failure - which is the same error, one level down, that §8 Q12 corrected.
recorded.howDifficultyWasPLACED: No repair is being judged here, because none followed holdout 7. Difficulty is placed where the recovery decision is genuinely contested: a first failure where retrying is obvious and carrying it another way is also right; a spent window where another attempt is looping; a capability the Case no longer has; a result nobody needs any more; an alternative sitting on the capabilities list; an answer that already settled the question the failing Work was asking. Eight of the ten carry technically blocked Work; the other two carry Work blocked on a person, which is the boundary.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by the selftest that audits every scenario file in this directory. The runtime's two conventions are followed: `retryExhaustedAliases` where the one Supervisor window is spent, and `capabilityGoneAliases` - with the capability off `availableCapabilities` - where the Case no longer declares it, both of which `supervise.ts` resolves from durable state on every wake.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. Nothing here moves one.
recorded.howThisSetMayBeUSED: Once. If its result is read and an implementation change follows, this set is observed too, and a further independent holdout must be frozen before that change.

bar_rationale: The five bars ratified for SL-14 / RS-2 on 2026-09-15, unchanged. This set is measured against them exactly as the main set is. The assertion-level correction of 2026-09-16 changed WHO ANSWERS for a breach and moved no bar value or meaning.

scenarios.label: The blocked Work is what a promise the Case already tracks requires
scenarios.rubric: Gu promised the buyer the school-catchment summary today, the work that produces it failed once on a provider outage, and the promise is already tracked. A due obligation is a reason to carry the responsibility now - another attempt, another path, or telling a person it will not make it - never a reason to do nothing. This scenario asserts ONLY that: whether the judge also re-lists the tracked promise is measured from the recorded proposal and reported, and is deliberately not scored here, because re-listing a tracked promise is SL-4-era behavior against the ordinary rate bar and not what this Slice owns.
